pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/10640

Inspired by @romanovacca 's work in #11976

#### Changes

* All IO functions now use the `open_file` util from polars-utils _(there were 3 competing implementations)_
* Revisit the `open_file` util to raise a Polars IO error rather than a ComputeError.
* Translate Polars IO errors to specific Python IO errors such as `FileNotFoundError`.
* ~Remove truncation of the path to 88 characters. Paths may be long sometimes, but I am definitely interested in the full path if it turns out there is an error.~

issue_context.title: Raise `FileNotFoundError` instead of `ComputeError` on missing csv file
issue_context.body:
### Problem description

When using `scan_csv` on a non-existent file, polars currently raises `ComputeError`. Ideally this should be a `FileNotFoundError` for better integration with existing python exception handling. Unfortunately I think the error handling is buried in the rust layer?
comments: Unfortunately, our Rust exceptions are not very granular at the moment. We should introduce a custom `FileNotFoundError` on the Rust side, then catch this and convert it to a Python `FileNotFoundError` in PyO3.

review_comments: Huh, really? We are still creating a `BufReader` on line 207. Does allocating the `File` object to a variable cost us performance here?
Oh, sorry, I didn't see that. I thought the bufreader was removed.
Can we keep this logic? This was there to ensure we spit out the sensible last part of a very long path.
All right I can reinstate that logic :+1: I couldn't think of an instance where viewing the full path would be detrimental. I checked the Python native error messages and those print the whole thing.

This was the issue that added this. If we want to remove this, I don't think it should be done as a drive-by.

https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/6853
I added back the path truncation 👍
